quest.title: Lonely Warrior
quest.description: Even if you had an army of ten thousand men, in the end, you must face this fight alone...\nStep forward... lonely warrior.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x550, Primogem x60, Mora x49200, Guide to Freedom x5, Hero's Wit x6, Mystic Enhancement Ore x11

chapter.title: To Those Who Embark on the Expedition

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Ugh...

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: ...The sword is unbroken? But I can't sense the Wolf Spirit...

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: (...Looks like I'm no longer in reality. This must be a space built from the entangled consciousnesses of Boreas and Roland.)

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: There's no way back, and all that lies ahead is the wolf's maw... Hmm...

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Hah, guess the only way is through.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Is this... the heart of the wolf?

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: ...! Roland!

dialogues.speaker: "Roland"
dialogues.text: ...I shall do as you wish, Knight of Boreas.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Huh... You're not quite how I imagined you. You don't seem half as crazed as the memories contained in the Wolf Spirit.

dialogues.speaker: "Roland"
dialogues.text: Not once have I strayed from the righteous path. But when I look at you... I do not see a hero capable of slaying dragons. Just a lost soul who has wandered far too long. A shadow of the knight you once were.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: I guess we have that much in common. Neither of us is at our peak.

dialogues.speaker: "Roland"
dialogues.text: The Rächer of Solnari's forces have been defeated, and the Roland you see is but an imperfect image cast by the Abyss.

dialogues.speaker: "Roland"
dialogues.text: I wield the power that Roland did at his peak, but my heart and mind remain frozen in that bloodstained moment.

dialogues.speaker: "Roland"
dialogues.text: Therefore, I, in my current form, am flawed... A knight cannot bear their own stagnation.

dialogues.speaker: "Roland"
dialogues.text: After redeeming you from injustice and guiding your surrender to the Abyss, I shall rectify myself and continue to follow the knightly path.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Hah! The world out there can bear no more of your torment. Your obsession, clearly, remains exactly as I had imagined. I suppose there's no chance to make you see the light?

dialogues.speaker: "Roland"
dialogues.text: No words can make a knight doubt his convictions, no matter how noble they may sound. Neither of us will sway the other... but you have long known this truth.

dialogues.speaker: "Roland"
dialogues.text: Otherwise, why would you pin all your hopes on Boreas's single thought?

dialogues.speaker: "Roland"
dialogues.text: But now the blade that once housed the Wolf Spirit has been shattered, and all you hold is a phantom that bears its form.

dialogues.speaker: "Roland"
dialogues.text: You no longer have the means to change the situation, and no one will come to your rescue... This place shall be your graveyard, lonely warrior.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Eh, maybe you're partly right... But I think I might just have a shot at a rescue.

dialogues.speaker: "Roland"
dialogues.text: ...What do you mean?

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: There's only one person's mind I need to change, and it isn't yours...

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Forgetting where we are? This is the heart of Andrius — God of the North Wind.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Andrius! Can you hear me?

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Wake up! You are the great God of the North Wind! How long will you allow yourself to suffer the domination of the Abyss?

dialogues.speaker: "Roland"
dialogues.text: ...If this is your final gambit, I am most disappointed, Knight of Boreas.

dialogues.speaker: "Roland"
dialogues.text: Grand displays of heartfelt wishes cannot summon miracles. This world shows no such mercy to its inhabitants.

dialogues.speaker: Andrius
dialogues.text: ...Return...

dialogues.speaker: Andrius
dialogues.text: ...Return to... the Ley Lines...

dialogues.speaker: Andrius
dialogues.text: ...This is my choice... my memory...

dialogues.speaker: Andrius
dialogues.text: ...Is this the answer that I found... at my journey's end?

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: And{RUBY#[D]Boreas}rius... At long last, I have delivered your token back into your heart.

dialogues.speaker: Andrius
dialogues.text: Heh... A Knight of Boreas? Watch on...

dialogues.speaker: Andrius
dialogues.text: ...This is all that a wo{RUBY#[S]I}lf can hope to do for human{RUBY#[S]you}kind...

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: ...On behalf of all humanity, I thank you, Lord of Wolves.

dialogues.speaker: "Roland"
dialogues.text: Boreas... is returning to the Ley Lines? But why? Your sword is broken — you no longer have the means to bear his soul... Unless... Surely not...

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Begging for miracles is a futile endeavor. I know better than that.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: ...But a sword is just one kind of vessel. There are other ways to store a soul.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: The Dominator of Wolves once bestowed the power of his soul upon his pack, strengthening their hearts and sharpening their claws and fangs.

dialogues.speaker: Boreas
dialogues.text: ...Even if it is not my intention, the soul of Lupus Boreas will inevitably ravage, devour, and assimilate a mortal heart... As if human and wolf were being forcefully merged into one being.

dialogues.speaker: "The Captain"
dialogues.text: ...If a mortal heart is to bear the soul of a god... This is a path that cannot be retraced. Yet I shall not dissuade a knight from embarking on the quest of his own choosing.

dialogues.speaker: "Roland"
dialogues.text: Your heart, your soul... they are collapsing? ...Ah, now I see.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: You were wondering how a lamb could tame the heart of a wolf... isn't that right?

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Here's my answer: You get the wolf to swallow the heart.

dialogues.speaker: "Roland"
dialogues.text: The Wolf Spirit within the sword was merely a decoy... the true thoughts and memories were carried within your heart.

dialogues.speaker: "Roland"
dialogues.text: To avoid arousing my suspicion, you deliberately allowed Lupus Boreas's soul to assimilate your own, then be devoured by me... But... how did you have the strength to fight while bearing such a great burden...?

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Compared to Lupus Boreas's decision... my sacrifice is nothing.

dialogues.speaker: "Roland"
dialogues.text: You have a stubborn will and employed an exceptional strategy... but this is not the way a true knight fights. The choice you have made is a flawed one.

dialogues.speaker: "Roland"
dialogues.text: Your soul is now merged with that of Andrius. When he fully joins the Ley Lines, you too will fall.

dialogues.speaker: "Roland"
dialogues.text: Neither Barbatos nor the Traveler will be able to anchor your soul from within the Ley Lines, let alone rescue you.

dialogues.speaker: "Roland"
dialogues.text: You have lost, and so have I. Regrettably, I can no longer offer you salvation.

dialogues.speaker: "Roland"
dialogues.text: ...May your soul rest in peace with Boreas, lonely warrior.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: ...Haha, lonely...?

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Sorry to disappoint you, but... As much as it sounded like the perfect ending, for both of us to return to the Ley Lines together...

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: The fact is that — unlike the true Roland of the past — I still have fine wine and good friends to get back to. They're looking forward to my triumphant return...

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: So I'm not ready to accept my fate just yet!

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Ding-dong! You've got mail!

talks.objective: Fight your way out of the Ley Lines

dialogues.speaker: Andrius
dialogues.text: ...Walk forward, and do not look back.

dialogues.speaker: Razor
dialogues.text: "Varka... Now, I know the meaning of my name."

dialogues.speaker: Rosaria
dialogues.text: "...After the lengths you've made everyone go for you, you'd better make sure to thank us all properly when you get back."

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: "You know, I have a lot of things to update you on... but they can wait until you're back."

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: "I have no intention of returning to the Knights of Favonius... But I trust you will find a way to manage on your own."

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: "...Grand Master, we're all waiting for you."

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Hmm? ...Oh. Heh.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: I'm... not doing too bad a job as Grand Master, am I?

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Heh... I'll take that silence as your approval.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Everything you swore to protect with your lives... It's all still here, safe and sound.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: The Knights of Favonius, Mondstadt... and the oath sworn by every knight. I'll protect them all with my life.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: And so... I'll deliver that letter on your behalf.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: ...I know it's just a shadow of the real Roland, but... if you have the time, could you please read it for him?

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Rostam and Arundolyn... They never forgot you.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Phew... This has been one long expedition.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: From here on out, I think I'll...

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: ...Let the wind lead.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: ...Hey, everyone. It's been a mighty long time.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: I'm... thrilled to see you all again.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Welcome back, Grand Master.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Yeah. I'm home.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Ahhh... It's been a while since I felt this wind on my face... Just how I remember. So, is there anything you'd like to talk about? Now's your chance, before I get dragged off to the office...

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: The sword was just a decoy — I carried his soul in my own heart... That was the plan I was most certain would work.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: The second half, though — using everyone's thoughts to guide me back out of the Ley Lines... I wasn't too sure that would work out, hah.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #All jokes aside, what would you have done if {NICKNAME} hadn't been able to separate the Wolf Spirit from Roland's influence?

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Hmm... Initially, I was planning to have Barbatos carry out that step. But when I approached him about it, he said there was a much more suitable candidate... The Outlander Who Caught the Wind.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: #Turns out our trust was not misplaced. Thank you, {NICKNAME}.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: But what if I'd failed?

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Then... I guess we'd have had to get Barbatos to send a wind to blow me back home?

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: ...But it would have come at a heavy price, and with no guarantee of success. Besides, I'd rather not have him expend that kind of power.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Hmm, it's a good question — a glass of the finest Dandelion Wine, perhaps? No doubt I'd have to pay for it with the secret stash of cash in my office.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You're dreaming if you think it would've come that cheap!

choices.text: ...How steep a price are we talking?

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Well, with the shadow of Roland vanquished, the Wild Hunt won't be able to consolidate their forces for the foreseeable future.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: A few knights will remain on rotation at the Nod-Krai stronghold, but everyone else will be sent home in waves.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Albedo and Durin will come back with the first wave, so you should have the chance to see them again soon.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: My future, huh... You may already have learned of this from Barbatos or the Hexenzirkel, but I glimpsed a reflection of the future in Barbeloth's scryglass.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You saw an Abyssal calamity in the North, right?

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Correct. Although, as things stand now... I believe we may have changed the course of the future — thanks in no small part to you.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Still, after I've tied up some loose ends with the Knights of Favonius, I'll need to make another trip back north... There's still a lot of work to be done at the Nod-Krai stronghold.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Besides, the first group of knights who volunteered to stay there have yet to be relieved of their duty. How could I simply abandon them?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Aw, how noble... But be honest, your main reason for going back to Nod-Krai is so you can dump all your work here on Jean again, isn't it?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Wait, seriously!?

choices.text: Aren't you gonna say something in your defense...?

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Haha. I'm only pulling your leg — you'll be seeing a lot more of me in Mondstadt from now on.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Alright then. I'm gonna stay here and enjoy the breeze for a little longer... For all the wine in the world, there's no feeling as intoxicating as the wind from your hometown after a long time away.

dialogues.speaker: "Roland"
dialogues.text: ...No matter the epoch, the world is awash with corruption and injustice.

dialogues.speaker: "Roland"
dialogues.text: Even the most fearless hero cannot fight what fa{RUBY#[S]death}te has ordained.

dialogues.speaker: "Roland"
dialogues.text: And even the holiest god cannot escape the shac{RUBY#[S]love}kles that bind them.

dialogues.speaker: "Roland"
dialogues.text: Lupus Boreas, if you still harbor love for humanity, then you must surely know...

dialogues.speaker: "Roland"
dialogues.text: There has only ever been one way to save them from injustice.

dialogues.speaker: Andrius
dialogues.text: ...Surrender to... the Abyss...
